text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Aston Villa and Fulham at Villa Park!

Aston Villa may have slipped up at Nottingham Forest last week, missing a chance to move into the Premier League's top four, but they bounced back straight away by beating AZ Alkmaar in the Europa Conference League on Thursday.

Now vying for a 13th top-flight home win in succession for the first time in 40 years, the Birmingham club have scored three goals or more in each of their five league games at Villa Park this season.
Today, Unai Emery's side can equal a club record of 21 Premier League victories in a calendar year.
After losing 1-0 at home to Manchester United last weekend, Fulham slipped further down the Premier League standings and they sit 16th ahead of today's game.
The Cottagers are yet to suffer consecutive league defeats in 2023-24, though, despite an apparent lack of firepower up front.
With a meagre tally of nine league goals so far this season, Marco Silva's men are also on a run of seven straight matches without scoring in the first half.
Villa make a trio of changes from their 2-1 win over AZ: the injured Diego Carlos is replaced by Pau Torres, while Matty Cash and Douglas Luiz come in for Clement Lenglet and Leon Bailey.
Tielemans retains his place, so Zaniolo must make do with a place on the bench.
Still seeking an end to his long Premier League goal drought, Raul Jimenez starts up front for Fulham, as Rodrigo Muniz is ruled out after injuring his knee last week.
Bobby De Cordova-Reid replaces Willian in the visitors' only other change.
Former Villa winger Traore is back on the bench following a layoff, but Issa Diop and fellow defender Tosin Adarabioyo remain sidelined.
The players are out on the pristine pitch at Villa Park, and kick-off is now just moments away!
Following a minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday, Fulham kick off, and we are under way in Birmingham.

After a fast-paced start to the game, Aston Villa try to seize control by keeping possession at the back, and an overhit back-pass temporarily has Yashin Trophy-winner Martinez in a little trouble before he calmly deals with it.
McGinn is perhaps fortunate to avoid an early booking after lunging into a challenge on Joao Palhinha in midfield.
He arrived too late and clearly caught the Fulham man, but only a free-kick is given.

SAVE! Villa have the first gilt-edged opening, as Diaby meets Digne's cutback near the penalty spot but can only sweep his first-time shot straight at Leno! The Fulham goalkeeper palms it away, and the visitors escape!
PENALTY FOR VILLA! Following Diaby's cross from the left, Watkins arrives in the centre of Fulham's box and turns the ball towards goal.

It's blocked by Castagne at close range, but seems to have touched the defender's arm! It's an early spot-kick for the Villans! However, the VAR has called the referee across to review it on the pitchside monitor!
NO PENALTY! After a brief review of the evidence, the referee concurs with his colleague in the VAR room and rules out Villa's penalty-kick! The ball did not touch Castagne's arm.
Fulham survive another scare!
The referee has certainly taken a lenient approach so far, as Jimenez mistimes a tackle from behind on Konsa but also avoids a yellow card.
Perhaps unsurprisingly, the hosts have had 72 per cent of the possession thus far, and their passing accuracy is some 20 per cent higher than Fulham's.
Aston Villa are a formidable team to conquer on home turf right now, and their latest visitors have started quite meekly.
Having been clattered by Konsa in a 50-50 challenge, Joao Palhinha is left in a heap on the soggy Villa Park turf, and the action is paused while he receives treatment.
Joao Palhinha is back on his feet now and resumes his role in Fulham's midfield, as Villa pick up where they left off and push forward again.

Villa are on a run of four straight home wins against Fulham - two in the Premier League and two in the Championship - while the London club's only league victory in their past 19 visits to Villa Park came back in April 2014.
The early evidence suggests those trends could continue today.
After Tielemans makes a superb sliding tackle deep in his own half, McGinn drives forward from midfield and some space opens up for Villa's captain.
However, his layoff to Diaby in the box is delayed just too long and the French forward's shot is blocked, before the assistant's flag is raised for offside.
After a swift passing move in the final third, Iwobi's cutback from the right byline picks out Pereira just inside Villa's area.
The latter's shot forces Martinez to dive across and make a sharp save, but Iwobi was offside in any case, and the hosts will have a free-kick.
Fulham are definitely growing in confidence now, having survived some early pressure.
However, Aston Villa's high defensive line does its job again, as Willian is caught offside just inside the home side's half.

VILLA LEAD! A teasing cross from the left by Tielemans zips across Leno's six-yard box, and after both Fulham's goalkeeper and Villa forward Diaby narrowly miss the ball, Robinson bundles it into the back of his own net - that's his second own goal of the season! The home side have made the breakthrough, and it's 1-0 just before the half-hour mark!
As Aston Villa have won every Premier League game they've taken the lead in this season - and Fulham have picked up just one point after going behind - the writing is perhaps on the wall already.
Still, there's plenty of time left to play at Villa Park.
A long ball over the top beats Villa's high line, and Pereira is almost clean through on goal; however, the ball skips up off the greasy turf and allows Konsa to make a last-gasp clearance.
His foot was quite high there, but the officials take no action.
Villa are still in control here, but Fulham are taking the occasional opportunity to probe the home side's defence.
The Cottagers' lack of first-half goals looks set to continue, though.
Covering across from left-back, Robinson does well to intercept a throughball from Douglas Luiz towards Diaby, and Fulham are holding firm.
SAVE! A superb diagonal ball by Pau Torres finds Cash on the right.

The Poland international drifts inside into a shooting position, just inside Fulham's box, but he is just off balance while striking the ball on his weaker foot and his effort flies straight at Leno, who deals with it comfortably.
The hosts are pressing hard for a second goal now, and Watkins claims for a foul deep in Fulham territory.
After his appeals are ignored, McGinn is then felled by Jimenez around 30 yards from goal in a central position - that's a Villa free-kick.

MCGINN MAKES IT TWO! Villa's captain doubles their lead just before the break! The Scottish star picks up possession from Robinson's headed clearance, and when space opens up he takes a couple of strides before finding the bottom-right corner with an unerring finish! That puts the home side in total control: 2-0!
Revelling in his freedom to break forward, McGinn has now contributed to goals in each of his last four home games in the Premier League - two of his own and two assists.
Villa have also scored 12 first-half goals in as many league matches, and only Manchester City (13) have netted more this season.
In the first minute of first-half stoppage time, Jimenez turns and sends a 20-yard snapshot curling towards the target.
It lacks enough pace or bend, though, and ends up as simple catching practice for Martinez.

Douglas Luiz sends a corner from the left towards Kamara on the edge of the area; although the Villa midfielder can't make useful contact, the ball then falls to Pau Torres, whose hurried shot is skewed well wide.
Willian cuts in from the left flank and puts Cash on the back foot, but his low curling shot from outside the area is easily fielded by Martinez, who drops down to complete the catch.
That's surely that for the first half.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 2-0 FULHAM
While not at their fluent best, Aston Villa have maintained their dominance of Villa Park during the first half, leaving Fulham floundering and perhaps bound for back-to-back defeats.
Apart from two tame efforts from distance, the visitors have posed their hosts little threat, and an own goal from Robinson followed by McGinn's precise strike puts Villa in charge at the break.

Unai Emery's side are unbeaten in 19 Premier League matches after taking the lead - including seven wins out of seven this season - so it would take an improbable Fulham fightback to stop them claiming maximum points today.
Fulham have now failed to score a first-half goal in 10 of their 12 Premier League fixtures this term, and only Luton Town (11) have failed to find the net more often before half-time.
Marco Silva's side have fared slightly better after the interval, though, so maybe getting a goal back early in the second half could bring them into contention for a point.
Fulham make one change for the second half, as they seek a route back into this game: De Cordova-Reid makes way for Wilson on the right wing.
Aston Villa kick off, and we are back under way in Birmingham!

OFF THE POST! Fulham almost pull a goal back early in the second half, but after Iwobi flicks a ball through for Jimenez on the right side of the box, the visitors' centre-forward sees his low driven shot tipped onto the far post by Martinez! Then, Willian skies his attempt from the rebound!
Another Fulham raid forward ends with Martinez making a more straightforward intervention this time, as Castagne's dangerous ball across from the right wing is cut out by Villa's goalkeeper.
Finally, the referee's patience expires, as Joao Palhinha is shown a yellow card for accumulated fouls.
He brings down McGinn in midfield, and a booking means he'll miss Fulham's first match after the international break.
Cash steps inside from the right, and after reaching the edge of the area decides not to play in a team-mate but instead curls a shot at goal.
Again, he barely tests Leno, who is able to pluck the ball out of the gloomy air.
There's no doubt that Fulham have improved markedly since half-time, and their latest attack concludes with Iwobi slashing a low strike well wide of the right-hand post.
The ball broke to him invitingly 20 yards out, but that was far from a confident finish.
Wilson now shoots off target, as the visitors continue to pose problems for a Villa side that has lost momentum since the interval.
Turning things on their head possession-wise, Fulham have had a 60 per cent share during the opening part of this second half.
They were starved of the ball before half-time, but that's all changed now.
Pereira's first-time ball across the box picks out Willian on the right.
The Brazilian winger skips inside before finding the side-netting with a low effort that prompts Martinez to make a precautionary dive down to his near post.
Perhaps troubled by Villa's loss of control, Unai Emery takes off Diaby and sends on Bailey to replace him.

VILLA HAVE THREE! Surely that finishes it!? On the counter, Bailey drives through open space and then McGinn holds the ball up well; Villa's captain flicks a return pass through for Bailey, who sends the ball along the box for Watkins to convert from close range.
That's the England striker's sixth Premier League goal of the season, and Villa extend their lead against the run of play: 3-0!
Bailey makes a brilliant impact from off the bench, as he propels his team forward on the break before setting up Watkins with an accurate cross.
For dissent in the aftermath of Aston Villa's third strike, Robinson adds a yellow card to his own goal - it's a day to forget for the Fulham full-back.
Soon after scoring Villa's third, Watkins clumsily clatters Bassey and is shown a yellow card by the referee.
Though Castagne steals the ball from McGinn deep in Aston Villa territory, he then loses the ball carelessly and the hosts break forward on a counter-attack.
However, it comes to nothing in the end.

FULHAM GET ONE BACK! Finally ending his 33-game Premier League goal drought, Jimenez prods the ball home from close range, after Robinson rolls the ball across Villa's six-yard box to tee him up! Fulham can still get something from this game, perhaps, as they reduce their deficit to two!
Released into the area, Robinson partly makes up for his own goal by completing a low pass to goalscorer Jimenez inside Aston Villa's area.
After the livewire Bailey zips inside from the right, Tielemans picks up possession and mishits a tame low shot straight at Leno, who makes a straightforward save.
Having hauled back Tielemans, who has proved a tough opponent in midfield, Iwobi becomes the latest player to receive a yellow card.
Aiming to continue their fightback by introducing some fresh legs, Fulham send on two more substitutes: first, the tiring Jimenez makes way for Carlos Vinicius.
Pereira is also withdrawn; Cairney comes on to replace him.
After Carlos Vinicius gets in behind the Villa back four, he forces a shot towards the near post, where Martinez has to make a smart save.
The flag then goes up for offside in any case, but Fulham are posing a regular threat now.

No less than 42 per cent of the action has taken place in Aston Villa's defensive third over the last 15 minutes - the hosts are under sustained pressure, but can they hang on to their lead until full-time?
Taking his chance to shoot from distance, Iwobi receives the ball from Willian and tests Martinez with a low shot skimmed along the turf.
It's ultimately a simple enough save for the Villa goalkeeper, though.
Marco Silva makes his final changes.
First, Iwobi is replaced by Reed.
Willian is also withdrawn, as ex-Villa winger Adama Traore sprints on to the pitch.
The referee decides Konsa is attempting to time-waste, so the Villa defender is booked.

OFF THE BAR! Villa almost grab their fourth goal! McGinn evades Bassey on the left byline, then cuts the ball back into the box; it strikes Joao Palhinha before spinning up onto Leno's crossbar - then Watkins somehow nods the rebound off-target.
Bailey then flashes a follow-up shot wide!!
After a frantic period of play at Villa Park, the action is momentarily paused as Bailey drops to the turf with what looks like a possible muscular injury.
He requires treatment from the medics.
Having been helped off the pitch, Bailey has been assessed and is fit enough to resume his role in Villa's attack.
We are back under way.
That's added a chunk of stoppage-time on to the end of this game.
At full stretch just outside his own area, Ream does well to intercept a raking pass by Douglas Luiz towards the lurking Watkins, who is keen to expose Fulham's stretched defence.
There will be at least seven minutes of added time at the end of this second half, as Aston Villa close in on their 13th straight home win in the Premier League.
Popping up on the left flank, Douglas Luiz drives into a dangerous position before flashing his cross just past several bodies inside Fulham's six-yard box; it eventually skips away to safety.
In the dying embers of the game, Carlos Vinicius is booked for a foul on Tielemans.
A clear pull on Tielemans' shirt results in Reed picking up a pointless yellow card.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 3-1 FULHAM
Relentless in their dominance at fortress Villa Park, Aston Villa post a 13th straight home win in the Premier League, seeing off struggling Fulham despite performing a little below their best.

Unai Emery's side cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time, but even after extending their advantage with a rapid counter-attack, their visitors continued to test them and deservedly notched a consolation strike as Jimenez scored his first league goal for well over a year.
The Villans start a league campaign with six successive home victories for the first time since 1959, and they will resume with a tough test at Tottenham after the international break.
Fulham, meanwhile, will host Wolves next time out, having suffered back-to-back defeats.
That's all from our live coverage today, so thank you for joining us and goodbye!
